definitions.explanation: Experiencing hunger, especially a deep or prolonged hunger. More evocative and literary than the everyday お{腹|なか}が{空|す}いた.

examples.japanese: ひもじい⟦{思|おも}い→思い：10248_omoi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{戦後|せんご}→戦後：12853_sengo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ひもじい⟦{日々|ひび}→日々：04804_hibi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}いた→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧。
examples.english: In the postwar period, days of hunger continued.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ひもじい⟦{思|おも}い→思い：10248_omoi⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦させたくなかった→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I never wanted to let the children go hungry.

notes:
USAGE:
Stronger and more emotive than ⟦お{腹|なか}→お腹：00805_onaka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{空|す}いた (I'm hungry). Often appears in narratives about poverty, wartime, or hardship. The set phrase ひもじい⟦{思|おも}い→思い：10248_omoi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to experience hunger / to go hungry) is the most common usage.

ETYMOLOGY:
Derived from ひもじ, a {女房詞|にょうぼうことば} (court ladies' word) for ⟦{飢|う}え→飢え：19826_ue⟧ (hunger), formed by taking the first syllable of ひだるい (hungry) and adding もじ.
